## Summary

The April 22, 2026 iOS and Android overview describes a customizable drop-in UI that determines available buy now, pay later (BNPL) plans and conditions, generates localized text, and displays it in the app. Both April platform sections use the same example image. The element presents potential terms. Rendering a message establishes neither financing approval nor payment confirmation, capture, or settlement.

![April 2026 mobile Payment Method Messaging Element example](../raw/assets/stripe-inapp-payment-method-messaging-element.png)

## November 2026 platform navigation

The November 7 base page keeps the same purpose and repeats an index with these three destinations:

- [iOS](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/payment-method-messaging-element.md?platform=ios)
- [Android](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/payment-method-messaging-element.md?platform=android)
- [React Native](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/payment-method-messaging-element.md?platform=react-native)

The index supplies routes. It gives no platform prerequisites, minimum dependencies, provider list, variant implementation, or general availability statement.

## Companion implementation and SDK scopes

The April overview linked to the separate [iOS Display BNPL messaging guide](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/display-bnpl-messaging.md?payment-ui=mobile&platform=ios) and [Android Display BNPL messaging guide](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/display-bnpl-messaging.md?payment-ui=mobile&platform=android). The retained [[source-stripe-inapp-display-bnpl-messaging]] source covers the April UIKit, SwiftUI, and Android examples. Its November index separately routes to those variants and React Native.

The April implementation examples use an existing Stripe account, a mobile SDK configured with a publishable key, a preview import on iOS, and a preview opt-in and separate `payment-method-messaging` dependency on Android. UIKit handles success with messaging content, no content, or failure. SwiftUI uses a view and phase-based display. Android uses a configuration result and Compose content. Those are messaging states, separate from authorizing a purchase.

The retained React Native 0.76.0 changelog records the April 29, 2026 announcement of **Public Preview** in 0.65.0. Independently, the retained `@stripe/stripe-react-native` 0.82.0 snapshot (`2026-10-21-6c2020d`) shows a root `PaymentMethodMessagingElement` export, a `configuration` prop, and an optional `onStateChange` handler for `loaded`, `loading`, `no_content`, or `failed`. Its component labels the feature Public Preview. These versioned records are separate from the November index and do not demonstrate general availability or device operation. See [[source-github-stripe-react-native]] and the companion implementation source for the exact typed configuration and the separately scoped Android font fix.

## Relation to Web Elements

The separate [[source-stripe-payment-method-messaging-element]] guide shows a Web Elements initialization with no `clientSecret`, lists Affirm, Afterpay/Clearpay, and Klarna within the captured web eligibility scope, and documents the web terms modal. These examples establish the captured Web Elements behavior. They do not supply native SDK or API floors, server credential requirements, a cross-platform provider list, or a universal PaymentIntent requirement.
